newsitem.title: GERMANY: Wall St lifts German DAX 1.6 pct at start.
newsitem.headline: Wall St lifts German DAX 1.6 pct at start.

text.p: German shares started the day with healthy gains on Thursday, getting a lift from overnight Wall Street gains.
The 30-share DAX index was up 67.43 points, or 1.55 percent, at 4,402.82 points at 0925 GMT. September DTB DAX futures were up 32.5 points at 4,420.5.
A series of well-received earnings reports from top German firms was underpinning the market.

Dealers looked for further gains during the session, but noted that volumes were relatively thin in many DAX component shares in IBIS computer dealings and said gains may be capped unless investor interest picks up.

Banking shares came back into vogue after weakening on Wednesday as Deutsche Bank AG was among the top volume shares, rising 2.65 marks to 119.35 marks, amid ongoing speculation about further banking industry mergers or takeovers.
Commerzbank AG, considered a top takeover target, was up 1.70 marks at 63.10.

Utility Veba AG gained three marks to 112.30 marks after reporting a rise in first-half net profit to 816 million marks from 743 million marks behind a rise in sales to 39.7 billion marks from 36.6 billion marks in the 1996 period.
Sportswear group Adidas AG surged 10.50 marks to 228.50 marks after reporting results on Wednesday.
Paribas Capital Markets raised Adidas to buy from no action, citing the outlook for Adidas to keep up high double-digit gains in sales and operating profit for 1997.
